reference_use.conclusion: SimonGMT provides blowUpMap, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt (Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) and support_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule. It has no locality, blow-up-point, derivative-fixing or orientation-invariance lemma, and neither does the snapshot project. Mathlib at the pin provides the facts the new children use: ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply (rfl), HasFDerivAt.isLittleO, eq_of_forall_dist_le and ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm. The assembly uses measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem, ae_restrict_iff' and ae_restrict_of_ae_restrict_of_subset. The DAG contains three comparator-accepted declarations whose statements are exactly the parent's steps 1, 3 and 5: imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null (d15b5cf), dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff (022bd01) and dsmc_att_blowUp_points_of_approxTangent (cb667a6). Their types match the accepted commits and their dependency closures are accepted, so they are reused. No accepted declaration covers step 6 or step 7. The related orient_comp nodes in other branches are unaccepted and have different, conjunctive types. The new names dtc_bc_lc_fderiv_apply_eq_of_approxTangent and dtc_bc_lc_unitOrientation_comp_eq collide with nothing. All child types elaborate in the comparator scope, and the frozen parent type follows from the four used child types. Both new children have complete Lean proofs. All of this uses only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

rationale:
Split into 5 children. Three are comparator-accepted declarations reused with their identical frozen types; two are new lemmas with the prefix dtc_bc_lc_.

Why split. Besides a.e. bookkeeping, the supplied proof makes five separable mathematical claims:
- (i) step 1: Hⁿ(M ∖ spt T) = 0;
- (ii) step 3: approximate tangent spaces are local and do not see null sets;
- (iii) step 5: points of T_xM are approximated by rescaled secants of the good set (test-function argument);
- (iv) step 6: a map that fixes a set pointwise and is differentiable at x fixes the approximate tangent plane at x;
- (v) step 7: a linear map that fixes an n-plane fixes its unit orientations.
Claims (i)–(iii) are already comparator-accepted DAG declarations with exactly these statements:
- imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null (minimizing_implies_stationary branch);
- dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff (density_and_tangent_cones.localize);
- dsmc_att_blowUp_points_of_approxTangent (density_one_implies_regular).
Without a split, this node's implementer may use only mass_eq_measure and vanish_off_support. It would have to re-prove all three, including the Hausdorff-measure test-function argument of step 5. Claims (iv) and (v) are new lemmas that other code can reuse; similar unaccepted orient_comp nodes exist in two other branches. Splitting them separates the analysis of step 6 from the multilinear algebra of step 7.

Children (parent step → child):
1. support_null / imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null (reused), step 1. The supplied step-1 argument through vanish_off_support and mass_eq_measure proves the identical claim. The accepted proof replaces it, so those two prerequisites are no longer needed.
2. tangent_local / dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff (reused), step 3.
3. blowup_points / dsmc_att_blowUp_points_of_approxTangent (reused), step 5 in unnormalised form: w ∈ Q is a limit of λ⁻¹(y − x) with y in the set and λ ↓ 0.
4. fderiv_fixes_tangent / dtc_bc_lc_fderiv_apply_eq_of_approxTangent (new; depends on blowup_points), step 6.
5. orientation_comp / dtc_bc_lc_unitOrientation_comp_eq (new), step 7.

How the children prove the parent. Steps 2 and 4 and the final assembly stay in this node.
Let μ := Hⁿ⌞(R.carrier ∩ O). R.carrier ∩ O is Borel because R.measurableSet_carrier holds and O is open.
(a) μ-a.e. x lies in R.carrier ∩ O (ae_restrict_mem).
(b) μ-a.e. x lies in T.support, because (R.carrier ∩ O) ∖ T.support ⊆ R.carrier ∖ T.support, which is null by support_null.
(c) μ-a.e. there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n R.carrier x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q. This is the field orients, restricted from R.carrier to R.carrier ∩ O.
Fix x satisfying (a)–(c).
- f x = x, because x ∈ T.support ∩ O.
- Put A := R.carrier ∩ (T.support ∩ O) ⊆ R.carrier. The set (R.carrier ∖ A) ∩ O ⊆ R.carrier ∖ T.support is null, x ∈ O and O is open, so tangent_local gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q.
- f is differentiable at x, because f is DifferentiableOn the open neighbourhood O of x. Also f fixes A pointwise and f x = x. So fderiv_fixes_tangent gives fderiv ℝ f x v = v for all v ∈ Q.
- orientation_comp with ξ = R.orient x and L = fderiv ℝ f x gives R.orient x (α.compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ f x)) = R.orient x α for every α.
The case n = 0 needs no separate treatment.

Checks.
- All 5 child types and the parent type elaborate in comparator challenge modules generated by verifier gmt-compare.py child_modules (contract mode). lean_contract.validate_lean_statement accepts all of them.
- A conditional Lean theorem with the four used child types as hypotheses proves the exact frozen parent type, using only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
- Both new children have complete Lean proofs using only these axioms (fderiv_fixes_tangent conditional on the blowup_points type). An end-to-end check proves the parent from the three reused types alone.
- The three reused types match their accepted commits d15b5cf, 022bd01 and cb667a6 after whitespace normalisation, and their dependency closures are all accepted.
- Neither new name occurs in dag.json (1061 nodes), in the run directory, in the snapshot, or under GMT/ in any git ref.
- An independent reviewer agent reproduced all of these checks and accepted the split.

subproblems.title: An integer multiplicity representation is carried by the support (reused accepted imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity representation of T in U (IMRep U n with R.Represents T, i.e. T(ω) = ∫_M θ⟨ω, ξ⟩ dHⁿ for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U)). Then Hⁿ(M ∖ spt T) = 0, where Hⁿ = μHE[n], M = R.carrier and spt T = T.support = U ∖ (zero region of T) (Simon 6.2.11).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), IsOpen U → R.Represents T → μHE[n] (R.carrier \ T.support) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration imrep_carrier_sdiff_support_null (DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.support_null-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit d15b5cf486116871dce9295932632b12f0af96e0). It is reused with its identical frozen type; a whitespace-normalised comparison with the declaration in that commit matches. Its dependency closure (imrep_carrier_inter_null_of_vanishesOn with its children lcn_covector_finiteDimensional, lcn_mult_mul_orient_apply_integrableOn and lcn_orient_apply_ae_eq_zero_of_vanishesOn, and imsupp_unit_orientation_ne_zero_norm_le_one) is accepted as well. Role in the parent proof: this is exactly the claim of step 1, Hⁿ(M ∖ spt T) = 0. The parent derives the same claim from vanish_off_support and mass_eq_measure; that second argument is not needed once this declaration is reused. The parent uses it in step 2. It shows that M' := M ∩ (spt T ∩ O) has full Hⁿ-measure in M ∩ O, and that (M ∖ M') ∩ O is Hⁿ-null, which is the locality hypothesis of tangent_local. The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source: this is the fact "μ_T(U ∖ spt T) = 0", used in step 2 of the parent proof (Simon 6.2.11 with 6.3.1; μ_T = θH^n⌞M by 6.3.2(3)).
1. Notation. M := R.carrier ⊆ U, θ := R.mult (θ ≥ 1 on M), ξ := R.orient, μ := μHE[n].restrict M. By definition T.support = U ∖ Z with Z := T.zeroRegion = ⋃𝒲, where 𝒲 is the family of open W with closure W compact, closure W ⊆ U and T.VanishesOn W (T ω = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W). Since M ⊆ U, M ∖ T.support = M ∩ Z.
2. Countable reduction. ℝ^P is second countable, so ⋃𝒲 = ⋃_k W_k for a countable subfamily (W_k) ⊆ 𝒲 (Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable). By countable subadditivity it suffices to show H^n(M ∩ W) = 0 for one fixed W ∈ 𝒲.
3. A finite measure. C := closure W is compact and C ⊆ U, so ∫_{M ∩ C} θ dH^n < ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult; since θ ≥ 1 on M, H^n(M ∩ C) < ∞. Put ν := μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C), a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P.
4. Orientation facts. By R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there are a plane Q and an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) spanning Q with ξ(x)(β) = s·β(τ_1, …, τ_n) for all n-covectors β, s ∈ {1, −1}. At such x: (a) |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ (operator norm of the continuous alternating map, since |τ_i| = 1); (b) ξ(x) ≠ 0: the n-covector β_τ(u_1, …, u_n) := det(⟨τ_a, u_b⟩)_{a,b} (for n = 0 the constant 1) is continuous, multilinear and alternating, and β_τ(τ) = det I = 1, so ξ(x)(β_τ) = s ≠ 0.
5. Testing T. Fix an n-covector α and set f_α(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(α). It is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (θ measurable, ξ a.e. strongly measurable for μ ≥ ν) and |f_α| ≤ ‖α‖θ ν-a.e., so f_α ∈ L¹(ν). For every g ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P, ℝ) with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ W, the form ω(x) := g(x)·α is smooth with compact support and tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport g ⊆ W ⊆ U, so ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport in W. As T vanishes on W and R represents T: 0 = T ω = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(g(x)α) dH^n = ∫ g f_α dν (the integrand vanishes off W ⊆ C).
6. Fundamental lemma. Mathlib's IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero (open set W, measure ν, f_α locally integrable on W) gives: for ν-a.e. x, x ∈ W ⇒ θ(x)ξ(x)(α) = 0. Since θ ≥ 1 on M and ν is carried by M, ξ(x)(α) = 0 for ν-a.e. x ∈ W.
7. Conclusion. Let α_1, …, α_m be a basis of the finite-dimensional space of n-covectors on ℝ^P. Intersecting the finitely many full-measure sets of step 6, for ν-a.e. x ∈ W the linear functional ξ(x) vanishes on a basis, hence ξ(x) = 0. By step 4(b), ξ(x) ≠ 0 for μ-a.e. x, hence for ν-a.e. x. Therefore ν(W) = H^n(M ∩ C ∩ W) = H^n(M ∩ W) = 0, and by step 2, H^n(M ∖ T.support) = 0.
proof_key_steps: M ∖ spt T = M ∩ zeroRegion(T), a countable union of open W ⊂⊂ U on which T vanishes.
Testing T with g·α (g ∈ C_c^∞(W), α a constant covector) gives ∫ g θ ξ(α) dH^n⌞M = 0.
The fundamental lemma of the calculus of variations gives ξ = 0 a.e. on M ∩ W, while unit orientations are nonzero; hence H^n(M ∩ W) = 0.

subproblems.title: Approximate tangent spaces are unchanged by removing a set that is null near the point (reused accepted dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M' ⊆ M ⊆ ℝ^P arbitrary sets, V ⊆ ℝ^P open, x ∈ V and Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P with Hⁿ((M ∖ M') ∩ V) = 0 (Hⁿ = μHE[n]). If Q is an approximate tangent space of M at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q: dim Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_Q φ dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x); Simon Ch. 3, 1.4), then Q is an approximate tangent space of M' at x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M M' V : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), M' ⊆ M → IsOpen V → x ∈ V → μHE[n] ((M \ M') ∩ V) = 0 → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration dtc_approxTangent_of_null_diff (DAG node root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.localize-a1.approx_tangent_local-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit 022bd01bf7500f65a1cfbba033ecf91be9652452, no dependencies). It is reused with its identical frozen type; a whitespace-normalised comparison with the declaration in that commit matches. Role in the parent proof: this is step 3 (locality of approximate tangent spaces; parent 7(a)). It is stated for an arbitrary open V instead of O and an arbitrary subset M' ⊆ M whose difference from M is null inside V. The parent applies it with M = R.carrier, M' = R.carrier ∩ (spt T ∩ O), V = O and x ∈ O. Here (M ∖ M') ∩ O ⊆ M ∖ spt T is null by support_null, and it gives HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q_x. The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source: Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4 (chapter-03.txt lines 77–85). This is the locality fact behind step 5 of the parent proof (orientation of M ∩ U') and step 6.6 (M_X and M_X ∩ K differ by an Hⁿ-null set).
Notation: μ := Hⁿ = μHE[n]; η_r := η_{x,r} = Chapter03.blowUpMap x r; for an arbitrary set A, ∫_A f dμ := ∫ f d(μ⌞A) (Mathlib's set integal). No measurability of A is needed below.
1. Reduction. The condition dim Q = n is part of the hypothesis and does not involve M. Fix f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). By hypothesis ∫_{η_r(M)} f dμ → ∫_Q f dμ as r ↓ 0. So it suffices to find r₀ > 0 with ∫_{η_r(M')} f dμ = ∫_{η_r(M)} f dμ for all r ∈ (0, r₀). The two functions of r then agree on (0, r₀), a set in the filter 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT), so they have the same limit (Tendsto.congr').
2. Choice of r₀. V is open and x ∈ V, so choose s > 0 with B_s(x) ⊆ V. tsupport f is compact, hence bounded, so choose L > 0 with tsupport f ⊆ B := B_L(0) (open ball). Then f(y) = 0 for y ∉ B. Put r₀ := s/L > 0 and fix r ∈ (0, r₀).
3. Cutting to B. For every set A ⊆ ℝ^P, ∫_A f dμ = ∫_{B∩A} f dμ. Indeed f vanishes off B, so ∫ f d(μ⌞A) = ∫_B f d(μ⌞A) (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). And (μ⌞A)⌞B = μ⌞(B ∩ A) because B is Borel (Measure.restrict_restrict).
4. η_r maps μ-null sets to μ-null sets. |η_r(a) − η_r(b)| = r⁻¹|a − b|, so η_r is Lipschitz with constant r⁻¹, and μH[n](η_r(N)) ≤ (r⁻¹)ⁿ μH[n](N) for every N ⊆ ℝ^P (LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le). μHE[n] = c·μH[n] with a constant c ∈ (0, ∞) (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def; addHaarScalarFactor_volume_hausdorffMeasure_ne_zero), so μ and μH[n] have the same null sets. Hence μ(N) = 0 implies μ(η_r(N)) = 0. Apply this to N := (M ∖ M') ∩ V, which is μ-null by hypothesis: μ(η_r(N)) = 0.
5. (B ∩ η_r(M)) ∖ (B ∩ η_r(M')) ⊆ η_r(N). Let y ∈ B with y = η_r(z) for some z ∈ M, and y ∉ η_r(M'). Then z ∉ M', since otherwise y ∈ η_r(M'). Inverting η_r gives z = x + r·y, so |z − x| = r|y| < rL < r₀L = s and z ∈ B_s(x) ⊆ V. Thus z ∈ (M ∖ M') ∩ V = N and y = η_r(z) ∈ η_r(N).
6. M' ⊆ M gives B ∩ η_r(M') ⊆ B ∩ η_r(M), so (B ∩ η_r(M')) ∖ (B ∩ η_r(M)) = ∅. With steps 4–5, μ((B ∩ η_r(M)) ∖ (B ∩ η_r(M'))) = 0. Hence B ∩ η_r(M') and B ∩ η_r(M) are μ-a.e. equal (ae_eq_set), and μ⌞(B ∩ η_r(M')) = μ⌞(B ∩ η_r(M)) (Measure.restrict_congr_set).
7. By steps 3 and 6, for every r ∈ (0, r₀): ∫_{η_r(M')} f dμ = ∫_{B∩η_r(M')} f dμ = ∫_{B∩η_r(M)} f dμ = ∫_{η_r(M)} f dμ. By step 1, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M' x Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: Only the blow-up integrals need checking. For f ∈ C_c pick L with spt f ⊆ B_L(0) and s with B_s(x) ⊆ V, and take 0 < r < s/L.
Each blow-up integral equals its integral over B_L(0). For such r, the parts of η_r(M) and η_r(M') inside B_L(0) differ by a subset of η_r((M ∖ M') ∩ V).
η_r is Lipschitz, so this set is Hⁿ-null. The restricted measures coincide, so the integrals agree for all small r and the limits are equal.

subproblems.title: Points of the approximate tangent plane are limits of blow-ups of the set (reused accepted dsmc_att_blowUp_points_of_approxTangent)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M, N ⊆ ℝ^P arbitrary sets with Hⁿ(M ∖ N) = 0 (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), x, w ∈ ℝ^P and Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P such that Q is an approximate tangent space of M at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, Simon Ch. 3, 1.4) and w ∈ Q. Then for every s > 0 there is λ₀ > 0 such that for every λ ∈ (0, λ₀) some y ∈ M ∩ N satisfies |λ⁻¹(y − x) − w| < s.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M N : Set (Euclid P)) (x w : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), μHE[n] (M \ N) = 0 → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q → w ∈ Q → ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → ∃ lam₀ : ℝ, 0 < lam₀ ∧ ∀ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam → lam < lam₀ → ∃ y ∈ M ∩ N, ‖lam⁻¹ • (y - x) - w‖ < s
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration dsmc_att_blowUp_points_of_approxTangent (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.mean_curvature_monotonicity-a1.approx_tangent_in_tangent_space-a1.blowup_points-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit cb667a61bedac01a38adc25c5277e01b9c79d4d4). It is reused with its identical frozen type; a whitespace-normalised comparison with the declaration in that commit matches. The two lemmas its proof cites are its accepted dependencies:
- plane_integral_pos = dsmc_att_setIntegral_submodule_pos (accepted, commit bf022843ec9b52d7f5f13d3dbed02e936ec53987). If finrank Q = n, g : ℝ^P → ℝ is continuous, compactly supported and ≥ 0, w ∈ Q and g(w) > 0, then ∫_Q g dHⁿ > 0.
- blowup_null_image = dsmc_att_blowUpMap_image_null (accepted, commit 7ba268af921b5ea14ebcb924406ff480f79ad705). If λ ≠ 0 and Hⁿ(E) = 0, then Hⁿ(η_{x,λ}(E)) = 0.
Role in the parent proof: this is step 5 (secant directions; parent 7(b)) in unnormalised form. Every w ∈ Q is a limit of λ⁻¹(y − x) with y ∈ M ∩ N and λ ↓ 0, instead of every unit v ∈ Q being a limit of (z_k − x)/|z_k − x|. The test-function argument is the same: a tent function at w replaces the cone function of step 5(c), and positivity of ∫_Q replaces step 5(d). The sibling fderiv_fixes_tangent applies it with M = N = A. The proof below is the accepted proof of this declaration, copied verbatim.

Source: parent proof steps 3, 5 and 6 (Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4). Uses the sibling children plane_integral_pos (Submission.dsmc_att_setIntegral_submodule_pos) and blowup_null_image (Submission.dsmc_att_blowUpMap_image_null).
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]. η_λ := blowUpMap x λ, so η_λ(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x). For S ⊆ ℝ^P, ∫_S f dHⁿ := ∫ f d(Hⁿ⌞S), where (Hⁿ⌞S)(B) = Hⁿ(B ∩ S) for every Borel set B (Measure.restrict_apply); S need not be measurable.
Fix w ∈ Q and s > 0.
1. Test function. Let g(y) := max(0, s − |y − w|).
 (a) g is continuous, g ≥ 0, and g(w) = s > 0.
 (b) If |y − w| > s then s − |y − w| < 0, so g(y) = 0. Hence g vanishes outside the compact set closedBall(w, s) and has compact support.
 (c) g(y) ≠ 0 forces |y − w| < s, i.e. {g ≠ 0} ⊆ ball(w, s).
 (d) Let f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P, ℝ) be g regarded as a compactly supported continuous map, so f(y) = g(y) for all y.
2. The limit is positive. HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q contains dim Q = n. Apply plane_integral_pos to Q, g and w (g is continuous, compactly supported and ≥ 0, w ∈ Q, g(w) > 0). This gives I := ∫_Q f dHⁿ = ∫_Q g dHⁿ > 0.
3. Choice of λ₀.
 (a) By the convergence part of HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt applied to f, F(λ) := ∫_{η_λ(M)} f dHⁿ tends to I as λ → 0 within (0, ∞).
 (b) Since I > 0, the open set (0, ∞) is a neighbourhood of I. So {λ : F(λ) > 0} belongs to the filter of neighbourhoods of 0 within (0, ∞).
 (c) Hence there is λ₀ > 0 with F(λ) > 0 for every λ ∈ (0, λ₀). Fix this λ₀ and let λ ∈ (0, λ₀).
4. The blow-up charges the ball. Put S := η_λ(M). Suppose Hⁿ(S ∩ ball(w, s)) = 0.
 (a) The ball is open, hence Borel, so (Hⁿ⌞S)(ball(w, s)) = Hⁿ(ball(w, s) ∩ S) = 0.
 (b) Since {f ≠ 0} ⊆ ball(w, s), the set {f ≠ 0} is Hⁿ⌞S-null. So f = 0 holds Hⁿ⌞S-almost everywhere, and F(λ) = ∫ f d(Hⁿ⌞S) = 0.
 (c) This contradicts F(λ) > 0. Hence Hⁿ(S ∩ ball(w, s)) ≠ 0.
5. The exceptional part is null. λ ≠ 0 (as λ > 0) and Hⁿ(M ∖ N) = 0, so blowup_null_image gives Hⁿ(η_λ(M ∖ N)) = 0.
6. Covering. Let z ∈ S ∩ ball(w, s); then z = η_λ(y) for some y ∈ M. If y ∈ N, then z ∈ η_λ(M ∩ N) ∩ ball(w, s). Otherwise y ∈ M ∖ N and z ∈ η_λ(M ∖ N). Hence S ∩ ball(w, s) ⊆ (η_λ(M ∩ N) ∩ ball(w, s)) ∪ η_λ(M ∖ N).
7. Suppose Hⁿ(η_λ(M ∩ N) ∩ ball(w, s)) were 0. Then step 6, monotonicity and subadditivity of the outer measure Hⁿ, and step 5 give Hⁿ(S ∩ ball(w, s)) ≤ 0 + 0 = 0, contradicting step 4. So Hⁿ(η_λ(M ∩ N) ∩ ball(w, s)) ≠ 0, and in particular this set is nonempty (the empty set has measure 0).
8. Take z in it. Then z = η_λ(y) = λ⁻¹(y − x) for some y ∈ M ∩ N, and z ∈ ball(w, s), i.e. |λ⁻¹(y − x) − w| = dist(z, w) < s. Since λ ∈ (0, λ₀) was arbitrary, λ₀ has the required property.
proof_key_steps: The tent function f(y) = max(0, s − |y − w|) lies in C_c, vanishes off ball(w, s), and f(w) = s > 0.
plane_integral_pos gives ∫_Q f dHⁿ > 0, so by approximate-tangent convergence ∫_{η_λ(M)} f dHⁿ > 0 for all λ ∈ (0, λ₀).
A positive integral of f over η_λ(M) forces Hⁿ(η_λ(M) ∩ ball(w, s)) ≠ 0.
blowup_null_image makes η_λ(M ∖ N) null, so η_λ(M ∩ N) ∩ ball(w, s) is nonempty. This gives y ∈ M ∩ N with |λ⁻¹(y − x) − w| < s.

subproblems.title: A map fixing a set pointwise and differentiable at x fixes its approximate tangent plane at x
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, A ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set, x ∈ ℝ^P and Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P such that Q is an approximate tangent space of A at x (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q: dim Q = n and ∫_{η_{x,r}(A)} φ dHⁿ → ∫_Q φ dHⁿ as r ↓ 0 for every φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), Hⁿ = μHE[n]; Simon Ch. 3, 1.4). Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be differentiable at x with f(x) = x and f(y) = y for every y ∈ A. Then Df(x)v = v for every v ∈ Q, where Df(x) = fderiv ℝ f x.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Euclid P) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q → DifferentiableAt ℝ f x → f x = x → (∀ y ∈ A, f y = y) → ∀ v ∈ Q, fderiv ℝ f x v = v
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 5–6 of the parent proof (parent 7(b)–(c): "Df(x) = id on Q_x"), stated for an arbitrary set A fixed pointwise by f. The secant-direction claim of step 5 is supplied by the sibling blowup_points (accepted dsmc_att_blowUp_points_of_approxTangent) with M = N = A, in its unnormalised form: points λ⁻¹(y − x), y ∈ A, approximate any w ∈ Q. Step 6 is then run with these points instead of the unit secants (z_k − x)/|z_k − x|. No case distinction in n is needed. If n = 0 then Q = {0} and the argument below is still valid.
Notation. Hⁿ := μHE[n]; |·| is the Euclidean norm of ℝ^P; L := Df(x) = fderiv ℝ f x, a linear map ℝ^P → ℝ^P with operator norm ‖L‖, so |Lz| ≤ ‖L‖|z| for every z.
1. Reduction. Fix v ∈ Q. It suffices to show |Lv − v| ≤ ε for every ε > 0, since then |Lv − v| = 0, i.e. Lv = v. Fix ε > 0 and put C := |v| + 1 > 0, K := ‖L‖ + 1 > 0, η := ε/(2C) > 0 and s := min(1, ε/(2K)) > 0. Then s ≤ 1, Ks ≤ ε/2 and ηC = ε/2.
2. Differentiability. f is differentiable at x with derivative L, so f(y) − f(x) − L(y − x) = o(|y − x|) as y → x. Applied with the constant η > 0, this gives δ > 0 such that |f(y) − f(x) − L(y − x)| ≤ η|y − x| for every y with |y − x| < δ.
3. Blow-up points. Apply blowup_points with M := A, N := A, the point x, w := v, the subspace Q and the radius s. Its hypotheses hold: Hⁿ(A ∖ A) = Hⁿ(∅) = 0; HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n A x Q is assumed; v ∈ Q; s > 0. It gives λ₀ > 0 such that for every λ with 0 < λ < λ₀ there is y ∈ A ∩ A = A with |λ⁻¹(y − x) − v| < s.
4. Choice of the scale. Let λ := min(λ₀/2, δ/(2C)). Then λ > 0 and λ ≤ λ₀/2 < λ₀. Take y ∈ A as in step 3 and put u := λ⁻¹(y − x). Then y − x = λu (as λ ≠ 0) and |u − v| < s ≤ 1. Hence
 (a) |u| ≤ |u − v| + |v| ≤ 1 + |v| = C;
 (b) |y − x| = λ|u| ≤ λC ≤ (δ/(2C))·C = δ/2 < δ.
5. The key estimate. Since y ∈ A, f(y) = y by hypothesis, and f(x) = x by hypothesis. By step 4(b), step 2 applies to y: |(y − x) − L(y − x)| = |f(y) − f(x) − L(y − x)| ≤ η|y − x|. Substituting y − x = λu and using L(λu) = λLu gives λ|u − Lu| ≤ η·λ|u|. Dividing by λ > 0 and using step 4(a), |u − Lu| ≤ η|u| ≤ ηC = ε/2.
6. Conclusion for v. |Lv − Lu| = |L(v − u)| ≤ ‖L‖|v − u| = ‖L‖|u − v|. By the triangle inequality,
 |Lv − v| ≤ |Lv − Lu| + |Lu − u| + |u − v| ≤ ‖L‖|u − v| + ε/2 + |u − v| = K|u − v| + ε/2 ≤ Ks + ε/2 ≤ ε/2 + ε/2 = ε,
 using |Lu − u| = |u − Lu| ≤ ε/2 (step 5), |u − v| < s (step 4) and Ks ≤ ε/2 (step 1).
7. Since ε > 0 was arbitrary, Lv = v by step 1. Since v ∈ Q was arbitrary, fderiv ℝ f x v = v for every v ∈ Q. ∎
proof_key_steps: Fix v ∈ Q and ε > 0; it suffices to show |Df(x)v − v| ≤ ε. Choose η = ε/(2(|v| + 1)) and s = min(1, ε/(2(‖Df(x)‖ + 1))).
Differentiability gives δ > 0 with |f(y) − f(x) − Df(x)(y − x)| ≤ η|y − x| for |y − x| < δ.
blowup_points with M = N = A and w = v gives, for the small scale λ = min(λ₀/2, δ/(2(|v| + 1))), a point y ∈ A with u := λ⁻¹(y − x) satisfying |u − v| < s; then |u| ≤ |v| + 1 and |y − x| < δ.
f(y) = y and f(x) = x turn the differentiability estimate, divided by λ, into |u − Df(x)u| ≤ η|u| ≤ ε/2.
The triangle inequality and |Df(x)(v − u)| ≤ ‖Df(x)‖|u − v| give |Df(x)v − v| ≤ (‖Df(x)‖ + 1)s + ε/2 ≤ ε, so Df(x)v = v.

subproblems.title: A linear map fixing an n-plane fixes every unit orientation of that plane
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P and ξ ∈ Λₙ(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P n, a continuous linear functional on n-covectors) a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q: ξ = ±τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τₙ, i.e. ⟨β, ξ⟩ = ±β(τ₁, …, τₙ) for all n-covectors β, for an orthonormal family τ spanning Q, with one fixed sign). Let L : ℝ^P → ℝ^P be a continuous linear map with Lv = v for every v ∈ Q. Then ⟨α ∘ ΛⁿL, ξ⟩ = ⟨α, ξ⟩ for every n-covector α, where (α ∘ ΛⁿL)(w₁, …, wₙ) = α(Lw₁, …, Lwₙ) is α.compContinuousLinearMap L.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ξ : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (L : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → (∀ v ∈ Q, L v = v) → ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, ξ (α.compContinuousLinearMap L) = ξ α
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 7 of the parent proof ("ΛⁿDf(x) fixes ξ(x) = ±τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τₙ"), stated for an arbitrary unit orientation ξ of a subspace Q and an arbitrary continuous linear map L fixing Q pointwise. The parent applies it with ξ = R.orient x, Q = Q_x and L = Df(x).
Notation. For an n-covector α (a continuous alternating n-linear map (ℝ^P)ⁿ → ℝ, Covector (Euclid P) n) and L, α ∘ ΛⁿL := α.compContinuousLinearMap L is the n-covector (w₁, …, wₙ) ↦ α(Lw₁, …, Lwₙ). In Lean, (α.compContinuousLinearMap L)(m) = α(L ∘ m) for every m : Fin n → ℝ^P (ContinuousAlternatingMap.compContinuousLinearMap_apply, which holds by rfl).
1. Unpacking. By definition of IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q there is a family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) : Fin n → ℝ^P, orthonormal, with span{τ₁, …, τₙ} = Q, and one of the two alternatives holds: (+) ξ(β) = β(τ) for every n-covector β, or (−) ξ(β) = −β(τ) for every n-covector β.
2. L fixes the frame. For each i, τᵢ ∈ span(range τ) = Q, so Lτᵢ = τᵢ by hypothesis. Hence L ∘ τ = τ as functions Fin n → ℝ^P.
3. The covector α ∘ ΛⁿL agrees with α on the frame. For every n-covector α, (α ∘ ΛⁿL)(τ) = α(L ∘ τ) = α(τ) by step 2.
4. Conclusion. Fix α. In case (+), ξ(α ∘ ΛⁿL) = (α ∘ ΛⁿL)(τ) = α(τ) = ξ(α), applying (+) once to β = α ∘ ΛⁿL and once to β = α. In case (−), ξ(α ∘ ΛⁿL) = −(α ∘ ΛⁿL)(τ) = −α(τ) = ξ(α) in the same way. Orthonormality of τ is not used. For n = 0, τ is the empty family and the same computation applies. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unpack IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q: an orthonormal frame τ with span Q and a fixed sign σ ∈ {±1} with ξ(β) = σβ(τ) for all β.
Each τᵢ lies in Q, so L ∘ τ = τ.
(α ∘ ΛⁿL)(τ) = α(L ∘ τ) = α(τ), hence ξ(α ∘ ΛⁿL) = σα(τ) = ξ(α) in either sign case.
